In determining the number of awards, DHS�s intent is to ensure beneficial competition occurs at the delivery order level while maximizing the effectiveness and efficiency of the BCD program. Proposal submission and evaluation details are provided within Sections L and M of this solicitation. Multiple Proposals Interested offerors may submit proposals for one or more of the five BCD award tracks. Each award track requires a separate proposal. Accordingly, an offeror that wishes to compete under multiple tracks shall submit a separate proposal for each track. Within a single track, an offeror may propose more than one device that satisfies the requirements of that track. In that case, the offeror shall include all proposed devices for that track within the single proposal submitted for that track. Basis for Award Proposals shall be submitted in accordance with the instructions outlined in Section L. There is no maximum number of IDIQ awards per track. These numbers are estimates, and DHS may increase or decrease the number of awards in its sole discretion. Using the HTRO-FRP award basis, the Government will evaluate the non-price factors to first determine the highest technically rated proposals beneath each track. If an offeror submits a proposal with multiple devices under a single track, each device will be separately evaluated and considered for award using a HTRO-FRP award basis. The Commercial Solutions Opening (CSO) authority is per Section 1823 of the National Defense Authorization Act (NDAA) for Fiscal Year 2026, which amended Section 3458 of Title 10, as codified by Public Law 119-60. DFARS Subpart 212.70 implements 10 U.S.C. 3458 for the acquisition of innovative commercial products or commercial services through the use of a general solicitation known as a Commercial Solutions Opening (CSO). This CSO is a competitive solicitation posted on a Government Point of Entry (GPE) www.sam.gov continuously open until 30 September 2027. This CSO will be utilized specifically for Watervliet Arsenal, and Benet Laboratories. ACC-WVA reserves the right to extend this CSO beyond the open until date by amendment. Under this CSO the DoW may seek solution briefs, presentations/pitches and/or proposals from traditional and non-traditional business entities. This CSO is intended to seek proposals for innovative commercial products, commercial technologies and services or adaptations/modifications of existing commercial product technologies and services to enable the seamless integration of manufacturing resources from across the enterprise to meet U.S. Army needs. This includes, but are not limited to, the linking of legacy analogue manufacturing systems with modern digital systems, the expansion of modeling and simulation to speed up decision making and the ability to deliver the right materiel solution to the soldier at the right time and in the right place. This CSO may result in the award of various types of contracts, which may include but are not limited to commercially-available technologies immediately available, commercially-available technologies fueled by commercial or strategic investment, but also concept demonstrations, pilots, and agile development activities that can incrementally improve commercial technologies, existing government-owned capabilities, or concepts for broad defense applications. ACC-WVA intends to award FAR-based contracts under Part 12 Commercial Item Procedures based on specific Area of Interest (AoI) and industrial base responses to the AoI. The CSO solicitation process may include a multi-phased solicitation and evaluation approach that is dependent upon specific AoIs. The AoIs are focused topic(s)/categories that will be published under this CSO. The following phases will be used: Phase 1 � Submission of Written Solution Brief, Phase 2 � Presentation/Pitch (if applicable), and Phase 3 � Request for Commercial Solution Proposal (CSP). A CSO is considered a competitive process, intended to ensure that competitive procedures are used to the maximum extent practicable. All solution briefs, presentations/pitches and/or proposals submitted in response to any AoI will be in response to and governed by this CSO. Use of a CSO in accordance with DFARS Subpart 212.70 is considered to be a competitive procedure for the purposes of 10 U.S.C. 221 and FAR 6.102. Finally, Contracting Officers shall treat items, technologies, and services acquired using a CSO as commercial items. Contracts or purchase orders resulting under this authority shall be fixed-price, including fixed-price incentive fee contracts. SOLICITATON NOTICE: The 700th Contracting Squadron (700 CONS) intends to award a Firm Fixed Price (FFP) purchase order on a sole source basis to Croner Group Limited (Cage Code: U1AA3); (Unique Entity ID: YL5XL93NM3Y8). This intended contract follows the guidance stated in the Department of Defense Manual (DoDM) 1416.08 which mandates compensation for local national personnel supporting U.S. Forces components in the United Kingdom to be based on salary and benefit data analysis. Consistency in the methodology and data source used for these studies is necessary to maintain year-to-year comparability and ensure changes in salary and benefits can be accurately measured. Croner Group Limited is the incumbent contractor under Contract No. FA561322P0008 and currently provides the salary and benefit data used to support this requirement. Croner utilizes established internal systems, methodologies, and historical data to provide consistent employment, wage, and benefit information to the Government. The current contract expires on 31 December 2026, and this follow-on acquisition is intended to ensure continuity of these services. In accordance with RFO 6.103-1, Croner Group Limited is the only responsible source capable of satisfying the Government�s requirement without substantial duplication of cost or unacceptable delays. Award to another source would require the Government and a new contractor to establish a new methodology and data baseline for the wage and benefit studies. This would disrupt year-to-year comparability with historical data and require additional time and resources to establish replacement processes. Additionally, transitioning to another source would create a risk of incompatibility between historical and newly collected salary and benefit data, which could negatively affect the Government�s ability to consistently evaluate changes in compensation. Croner�s established processes and historical data provide the continuity necessary to support the Government�s compensation analysis. Accordingly, the Government intends to solicit and award to Croner Group Limited as the only responsible source capable of meeting this requirement. This notice is not a request for competitive quotes. However interested parties may submit a capability statement upon the referenced deadline within the attached solicitation (FA561327Q0001) demonstrating their ability to perform the requirement described herein. Upon receipt of any such notifications, the Contracting Officer will determine whether to conduct a competitive procurement or proceed with sole source action. Responses received will be reviewed, however; a determination by the Government not to compete the proposed procurement based upon responses to this notice is solely within the discretion of the Government. If no responses are received, the 700 CONS will proceed with the sole source award to Croner Group Limited. See attached solicitation (COMBO-SOLICITATION FA561327Q0001)

The Regional Maintenance Center at Puget Sound Naval Shipyard and Intermediate Maintenance Facility (PSNS and IMF) intends to award a stand-alone Firm-Fixed-Price contract to accomplish maintenance, repair, and preservation of YRBM-50. The YRBM-50 characteristics are Length: 153FT, Width: 43FT, Age: 82 Years, Hull Type: Steel, Draft: 6FT, Full Displacement: 900 L Tons and Light Load: 427 L Tons. The Contractors facility must possess the capability of YRBM-50 with the dimensions as stated above. To facilitate proper government oversight, the facility shall be located in the Puget Sound, WA region. For this procurement, the Puget Sound, WA region is defined as the West Coast of the continental US, starting from Olympia, WA and extending northward to Bellingham, WA. Scope Overview: Coordinate with the Contracting Officer, via the SUPERVISOR to deliver the vessel to the Contractors facility. To facilitate proper government oversight, the facility where the work will be performed shall be located in the Puget Sound, WA region. For this procurement, the Puget Sound, WA region is defined as the west of the continental US, starting from Olympia, WA and extending northward to Bellingham, WA. Upon docking vessel, wash, and clean vessel. Accomplish required inspections and fender repairs. Remove existing and install new zinc anodes. Hull, freeboard and exterior decks require ultrasonic measurement of plating thickness and repair of areas below minimum thickness as needed. Accomplish blast and paint preservation of hull, freeboard, exterior decks and superstructure. Vessel requires inspection for damage and deterioration (hull, exterior decks, and tanks/voids plating and framing). Apply new non-skid system to exterior decks. Open, clean, ventilate, inspect, test, and maintain dry each tank/void. Accomplish partial preservation of QTY (24 EA) ballast tanks/voids. Accomplish access cover and watertight hatch and door repairs. Disinfect and certify potable water system. Pump and clean the interior surfaces of the CHT tank. Accomplish main deck repairs, hawse hole bulls eye and bolster repairs, and hull fendering system modifications. Accomplish the following modifications: hot water heater installation, awning replacement, A/C plant replacement and backup systems, switchboard upgrades, 1MC replacement and phone system upgrades, and CCTV upgrades. The aforementioned contractor is currently performing under contract number 36C24226A0010 with the period of performance concluding on September 30, 2026. The anticipated period of performance for the bridge award is six (6) months, from October 1, 2026, through March 31, 2027, with one (1), six (6) month option period. The bridge award will be made under the authority of Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) GSAM 538.7104-3(b)(ii); only one source is capable of providing the products and services required at the level of quality required because the products and services are highly specialized. As written, the DVAs requirement for molecular testing is able to be fulfilled through GSA s Federal Supply Class (FSC) Group 66 III. FSC Group 66 III, 605-6B was established for the procurement of clinical immunochemistry analyzers and corresponding tests and supplies; this group is a priority strategic source under Revolutionary FAR Overhaul (RFO), and General Services Acquisition Regulations (GSAR) procedures, and as supplemented by the Veterans Affairs Acquisition Regulations (VAAR). A long-term action was competitively awarded under FSC Group 66, from solicitation 36C24226Q0487 on a Cost Per Test (CPT) basis. Blanket Purchase Agreement (BPA) 36C24226A0041 was awarded to Roche Diagnostics on July 1, 2026. A bridge action is required to ensure continued CPT molecular testing, allowing Roche Diagnostics sufficient time to deliver, install, and validate the new analyzers under BPA 36C24226A0041, subsequently removing the current analyzers after validation (36C24226A0010). USCIS requires timely, scalable, and intelligence-driven capabilities to support the identification of potential fraud indicators and enhanced vetting activities involving individuals throughout the USCIS immigration lifecycle. The required capability must support batch processing of Government-provided target records; identity resolution and corroboration using authoritative commercial and publicly available information; identification and correlation of publicly available online identities and digital activity associated with target records; application of USCIS-designated review criteria; and source documentation sufficient for analyst validation and Government review. Contractor-provided information will support Government analysis and will not constitute an adjudicative, eligibility, enforcement, or adverse-action determination. In accordance with FAR 5.101(c)(4)(vii), based on the market research conducted, the Government intends to award this requirement on a noncompetitive basis to Thomson Reuters Special Services LLC (TRSS). The Government identified sources capable of providing discrete capabilities, including social-media screening, public-record research, identity intelligence, and investigative data support. Force plate analysis is a common method by which human gait and balance can be accurately quantified. All cables and accessories required for synchronization should be included. O Generates digital output of at least six measurement channels (described above) that uses a single USB cable to connect with an acquisition computer running Windows 10 and is easily integrated in Vicon Nexus 2.X software. o Compatible with Vicon Nexus software versions 2.6 through 2.19 (or latest available version) o Includes necessary drivers, plugins, or SDK components for integration o Real-time data streaming capability to Vicon Nexus environment o Includes at least 15-foot USB cable for power and data transfer o Force plates allow for user selectable digital data rates between 10-1000 datasets per second. o Force plates do not require an external amplifier. Amplifier must be bult into the force plate. o Force plate dimensions are no greater than 51 x 51 x 4.6 centimeters with a 300-pound (or greater) vertical force capacity. o Force plate is portable such that it does not require any mounting and weighs less than 12 kilograms. o Hardware solutions are provided to recess the force plates into raised flooring such that data accuracy and integrity are not compromised. Originally built on a baseline commercial Impresa MRO/ERP software foundation, the system has undergone extensive, continuous customization over the past 24 years. These modifications enable real-time communication with 17 legacy Department of Defense (DoD) systems. This highly specialized, proprietary configuration of the COTS software bears little structural resemblance to its commercial progenitor and operates as a unique hybrid system. MABSM operates and is sustained within the Department of the Air Force's Cloud 1 enterprise cloud environment, leveraging DoD Impact Level 4/5 (IL4/IL5) secure cloud infrastructure. Sourcing specialized contractors who can operate seamlessly within Cloud 1's DevSecOps frameworks, managed services, and security boundaries is crucial to system stability. MABSM dictates the real-time tracking of critical assets, including aircraft parts, financial transactions, and Nuclear Weapons-Related Material (NWRM) items. Due to the high-tempo depot environments in which it is deployed, the system requires a performance baseline exceeding 95% system uptime and near-zero code degradation. Furthermore, national security mandates dictate 100% real-time accountability of NWRM items within any given 24-hour period. TIDAL: Target-Induced Droplet Assembly of Ligands

Developed by Los Alamos National Laboratory, TIDAL (Target-Induced Droplet Assembly of Ligands) transforms the small antibody fragments known as nanobodies into a programmable, protein-only material that organizes itself on demand. By harnessing a natural process called liquid-liquid phase separation, TIDAL lets these binders gather into dense, dynamic droplets precisely when they encounter their intended target, giving developers a single platform that can purify proteins without costly resins, deliver drugs as a self-forming slow-release depot and even trap harmful proteins inside living cells. The outcome is a versatile toolkit that lowers production costs, simplifies manufacturing and opens fresh therapeutic and diagnostic possibilities, all from a building block that biology already knows how to make. Overview At the heart of TIDAL is a small, engineered tag, called an encapsulation peptide (EP), that is fused to a nanobody. When many of these tagged nanobodies are present, they undergo liquid-liquid phase separation, similar to what makes oil bead up in water, and they collect into concentrated liquid droplets made entirely of protein. Binding to the target molecule intensifies the effect, so the droplets form most strongly exactly where and when that target is present. Because the assembly is dynamic and reversible, the droplets behave as stimuli-responsive materials whose thickness and flow can be tuned by the target ligand, allowing one design to serve as a purification handle, a delivery vehicle or an intracellular trap. Technology Description TIDAL: Target-Induced Droplet Assembly of Ligands treats the nanobody itself as a structural component rather than merely a binding reagent. Each fusion polypeptide pairs a target-specific nanobody with the encapsulation peptide (EP), and it is the peptide that drives the many weak, cooperative interactions responsible for phase separation. In solution these interactions produce biomolecular condensates, dense droplet phases that concentrate the nanobodies far above their ordinary levels; the presence of the matching ligand pushes the balance further toward condensation. Because condensation is governed by many cooperative contacts rather than a single rigid bond, the droplets stay liquid-like and dynamic, and their formation can be reversed when the trigger is removed. Building on that behavior, the droplets function as programmable modules for delivery, stability or signal enhancement. Their rheology, meaning how readily they flow, can be switched by the target ligand, so a preparation can remain fluid enough to pass through a fine needle yet convert into a slow-release depot once injected. The same concentrating power lets the droplets scavenge and enrich internalized components to levels far above normal, which sharpens detection in diagnostics, and, when produced inside cells, the condensates can sequester disease-driving proteins such as oncogenic or viral factors into synthetic granules that block their activity. Purification follows the same logic: Triggering condensation precipitates the bound target out of solution, offering a resin-free alternative to the slow and expensive column methods used today. Advantages Cuts protein purification costs by replacing slow, expensive column resins with a simple trigger-and-precipitate step Enables patient-friendly, at-home injections that stay liquid in the syringe then set into a slow-release depot Works entirely from protein, avoiding synthetic carriers and easing manufacturing Can operate inside living cells to trap and neutralize harmful proteins linked to cancer or viral infection Boosts diagnostic sensitivity by concentrating faint signals into detectable droplets Offers one adaptable platform spanning manufacturing, therapy and detection Market Applications � Biopharmaceutical Manufacturing (antibody and enzyme purification, protein production) � Therapeutics and Drug Delivery (subcutaneous slow-release treatments, intracellular protein targeting) � Diagnostics (high-sensitivity detection assays, point-of-care testing) � Biotechnology (resin-free enzyme immobilization, biocatalysis) � Reagents (protein capture, condensate-based cell studies) TRL 3 U.S. Patent pending LA-UR-26-27937 LANL Tech Partnerships: Unlock the Innovative Potential Los Alamos National Laboratory offers a wide range of cutting-edge technologies and capabilities that may provide your company with a competitive edge in the market and unlock the innovative potential that can enhance, refine, and revolutionize your products. B--Intent to Award Notice: University of Minnesota

The U.S. Geological Survey (USGS), Florence Bascom Geoscience Center, intends to award a non-competitive purchase order to Regents of the University of Minnesota, University of Minnesota (U of M), located in Duluth, MN, for a suite of geochemical analyses on water and sediment samples in direct support of the research project, Drought and Flood Extremes of the Continental United States: Past to Present., to be delivered to Reston, VA for the period of 9/21/2026 to 9/20/2027 with four (4) Option Years as follows: Option Year One (1): 09/21/2027 - 09/20/2028 Option Year Two (2): 09/21/2028 - 09/20/2029 Option Year Three (3): 09/21/2029 - 09/20/2030 Option Year Four (4): 09/21/2030 - 09/20/2031 The study conducted in this research project necessitates freeze coring to preserve the structure of mm-scale, water saturated seasonally-deposited layers. The only way to ensure preservation of these layers is by flash freezing the sediments at the bottom of the lake and keeping the "freeze core" completely frozen during transport and analyses. The U of M offers the only nearby facility where the frozen cores can be stored and analyzed over the duration of the five-year research project, which allows for short transport in a cooler on dry ice from each of the six to twelve study sites, where each core is collected. Transport between the study sites or frozen storage must be within a 200-mile radius and a few hours' drive in order to keep the samples firmly frozen during transport. The U of M is the only facility within the required radius offering stable isotope, elemental abundance, mineralogy, or major ion measurements of environmental samples. Analyzing a frozen core at the micron scale on an x-ray fluorescence scanner takes 6-8 hours, which would ordinarily result in melting. UMD has previously co-developed a distinctive method for scanning a frozen core. As a result, UMD and the technical staff are uniquely capable of carrying out these analyses without destruction of the freeze cores, as required. The University of Minnesota also provides in-kind support in the forms of unique specialized expertise of stable isotopic processes, student and technician time, and facility and equipment access. Objectives The objectives of this contract are to: Enhance participants� ability to make sound decisions under pressure by analyzing historical leaders� actions at Gettysburg. Requirements and Tasks The Contractor shall perform the following tasks: Program Design and Curriculum Development Develop a customized curriculum that incorporates a three?phase staff?ride methodology (preliminary study, field study, and integration) or equivalent structure appropriate for leadership development. Period of Performance The period of performance for this contract shall be 30 days from date of award. The units will be provided by Rugged Controls LLC, located at 4211 24th Avenue West, Seattle, WA 98199. NOAA�s Office of Marine and Aviation Operations manages and operates a fleet of oceanographic survey and fisheries science ships. These vessels use winch control displays manufactured by MTNW or Rugged Controls. Rugged Controls purchased MTNW in 2014, and the RPC-90x is the current replacement for the legacy Lci90 units used throughout the NOAA fleet. The intended use is to provide stable and accurate winch wire tension information used by the science community, deck departments, and vessel pilots. Accurate information regarding the location of underwater packages in the water column, winch tension, and angle is critical to mission science, safe navigation, personnel safety, and equipment safety. Other manufacturers� products would require a completely new installation and mounting arrangement, as well as training for both users/operators and maintainers. The RPC-90x is nearly identical to the equipment currently installed throughout the NOAA fleet and can be installed with minimal changes. Use of another manufacturer�s system would result in additional engineering, training, installation, and review requirements and could require the vessel to be dockside for an extended period. Rugged Controls is the Original Equipment Manufacturer (OEM) of the RPC-90x and holds proprietary rights to the design and configuration of these winch control displays. Market research identified other manufacturers of winch control displays; however, no other source was identified that possesses the required technical knowledge or integration rights to provide the required Rugged Controls equipment with the necessary compatibility, parts, and technical support. The Government is not aware of any other vendors that can provide the required Rugged Controls RPC-90x units while maintaining compatibility with the existing NOAA fleet systems. THIS IS NOT A REQUEST FOR PROPOSALS, AN INVITATION FOR BIDS, OR A REQUEST FOR QUOTATIONS. This is a Sources Sought Notice (PUR260176) with the intent to award a sole source purchase order to Avenca, Ltd (AVENCA), under the authority of FAR 13.106-1 based on their unique technical qualifications as the developer of the Marine Accident Data Analysis System (MADAS) suite of software products. The National Transportation Safety Board (NTSB) knows of no other sources for this requirement. Notice is provided as information to the marketplace, market research, and is an invitation for any other qualified companies to express their interest in and demonstrate their capability to provide the required work. The National Transportation Safety Board (NTSB) is an independent federal agency charged by Congress with investigating every civil aviation accident in the United States and significant events in the other modes of transportation�railroad, transit, highway, marine, pipeline, and commercial space. We determine the probable causes of the accidents and events we investigate and issue safety recommendations aimed at preventing future occurrences. In addition, we conduct transportation safety research studies and offer information and other assistance to family members and survivors for each accident or event we investigate. We also serve as the appellate authority for enforcement actions involving aviation and mariner certificates issued by the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) and US Coast Guard, and we adjudicate appeals of civil penalty actions taken by the FAA. The NTSB Office of Research and Engineering, Vehicle Recorder Division (RE-40) currently uses the MADAS software suite to perform Voyage Data Recorder (VDR) analysis. The suite contains several modules that allow parsing, decoding, and replay of data recovered after a marine accident. This requirement to increase the capabilities of the National Marine Electronics Association (NMEA) Parser module of the MADAS suite will expand the types of data able to be parsed and allow the data to be parsed more expeditiously, decreasing the amount of time required to analyze a VDR dataset. The period of performance of the requirement is one (1) year from the date of award. The decision to award a sole source order is based on the fact that AVENCA is the developer of the MADAS suite of software products and the only known source capable of providing enhancements to existing modules due to its proprietary software development. Amendment 0001- Conex Refurbishment, Officer Training School (OTS), Maxwell AFB

Statement of Requirements Conex Refurbishment, Officer Training School (OTS), Maxwell AFB Purpose: The purpose of this requirement is to obtain comprehensive restoration services for 27 Conex containers located at the Vigilant Warrior (VW) training site. The restoration is necessary to eliminate significant safety hazards posed by severe wood deterioration, restore the environmental integrity of the containers, and ensure their operational effectiveness for training over 5,000 cadets annually. Description of Items: The contractor shall provide all necessary personnel, supervision, materials, equipment, tools, and services to perform complete restoration and repair of the 27 Conex containers. The work includes, but is not limited to, the following: Structural Component Restoration Assess and replace all deteriorated wood framing, flooring, and structural elements. Ensure all replacement materials meet or exceed original load-bearing specifications and comply with military construction standard UFC 1-200-01. All structural modifications must be certified by a licensed structural engineer. Window and Door Frame Restoration Restore window and door frames to provide a complete weatherproof seal when closed. Hardware must enable secure locking mechanisms to prevent unauthorized access. Materials used must resist corrosion and deterioration in outdoor environments. Environmental Protection Systems Achieve complete weather resistance to prevent water, snow, and wind infiltration. All joints, seams, and penetrations must be properly sealed. All openings must be sealed to prevent the entry of rodents, birds, and insects. Delivery Requirements: The contractor shall provide a detailed construction phasing plan to the government for approval. The plan must ensure that a minimum of 70% of the containers remain operational at all times. No more than 12 containers may be out of service simultaneously without prior government approval. The work will be performed on-site at the Vigilant Warrior training site located in Elmore County, Alabama. The address is: 407 Lakeland Drive, Titus AL. Installation Requirements: The contractor will be responsible for the installation of all new materials and components as part of the restoration services. When material replacement is required, the contractor shall procure and install materials as per specifications approved by Officer Training School (OTS). Standard Warranty: The contractor shall provide any Original Equipment Manufacturer (OEM) standard commercial warranty applicable to the products being purchased at no additional cost to the Government. Warranty shall include, as a minimum, technical support, troubleshooting assistance, and replacement of faulty equipment. The contractor must provide a 48-hour response for any warranty issues that affect training operations. All materials shall demonstrate a minimum 15-year service life, with a manufacturer's warranty of a minimum of 10 years on primary structural components. Prior to project acceptance, the contractor shall provide the customer with all manufacturer warranties as needed for any component incorporated into this project such as equipment manuals, literature, and other documentation on all equipment. Prior to project acceptance, the contractor shall provide the written procedures, points of contact within the company, and required information for all warranty services prior to project acceptance. This information shall include written confirmation of the warranty period, phone numbers and contact information/procedures for technical support, troubleshooting assistance, and replacement of faulty equipment. General Information: Items must be brand new. Refurbished items are not authorized. Reporting: The contractor is required to provide monthly progress reports detailing progress, materials used, quality control activities, and any safety incidents. Quality Control: The contractor shall establish and maintain a Quality Control Program. A Quality Program Plan (QPP) must be submitted within 30 days of contract award. This program will include inspection hold points at 25%, 50%, and 75% completion for each container, with government inspection rights at each phase. USCG - Response Boat, Small Third Generation (RB-S III)

The United States Coast Guard (USCG) has an upcoming requirement to design, build, test, and deliver the Response Boat, Small Third Generation (RB-S III). This acquisition recapitalizes the aging fleet of 29-foot Response Boat-Small Second Generation (RB-S II) platforms approaching their end of service life. The contractor will provide the boats, trailers, full logistics support, technical documentation, configuration management, and supply support. The RB-S III will be a commercial product designed to execute multiple missions, including Search and Rescue (SAR); Ports, Waterways, and Coastal Security (PWCS); Migrant Interdiction (MI); and Other Law Enforcement (OLE). The Government anticipates procuring up to 400 RB-S III boats for the USCG and an additional 100 modified RB-S III variants for other Federal Government agencies, subject to final requirements, availability of funding, and applicable ordering authority. The Government anticipates awarding up to four (4) Indefinite Delivery, Indefinite Quantity (IDIQ) contracts. The resulting delivery orders are anticipated to utilize Firm-Fixed-Price (FFP) and Fixed-Price with Economic Price Adjustment (FP-EPA) line items, as identified in the solicitation. The anticipated IDIQ ordering period is ten (10) years, consisting of a five (5) year base ordering period and one five (5) year option ordering period. Primary production will take place at the respective contractors' facilities. Delivery will take place at various USCG locations across the continental United States which will be specified in the solicitation. The solicitation is anticipated to be released by the end of Fiscal Year (FY) 26. The Government anticipates providing approximately 45 calendar days for submission of proposals. Formal Question and Answer procedures, including deadline for submission of questions, will be identified in the solicitation. Contract awards are anticipated in the second quarter of FY 2027. The Government anticipates conducting this competitive procurement using a two-phase acquisition methodology: Phase I - Offerors will submit initial technical, management, and conceptual design proposals. The Government will evaluate the Phase I submissions in accordance with the evaluation criteria established in the solicitation and anticipates award of up to four (4) IDIQ contracts. Each IDIQ awardee will proceed to Phase II. Phase II - Each Phase I IDIQ awardee will be issued an initial delivery order satisfying the minimum guarantee under its IDIQ contract to complete the detailed construction/production design, build one (1) demonstration vessel, and participate in a Government-conducted In-Water Demonstration. The Government will evaluate the results of each demonstration vessel in accordance with the Phase II evaluation methodology established in the solicitation. Following completion of the Phase II evaluation, the Government anticipates selecting one (1) IDIQ contractor to receive subsequent RB-S III production orders during the remaining ordering period. The final ordering structure and procedures will be established in the solicitation and resulting contracts. The anticipated solicitation will provide the specific Phase I and Phase II evaluation criteria, evaluation methodology, and basis for selecting the IDIQ contractor anticipated to receive subsequent production orders. Modernization and Engineering Support - III (MES III)

The Air National Guard (ANG) Air Force Reserve Command Test Center (AATC) is a unit of the ANG stationed at Tucson Air National Guard Base (ANGB), AZ with operating locations at Davis-Monthan Air Force Base (AFB), AZ; Eglin AFB, FL; Little Rock AFB, AR; Roland R. Wright ANGB, UT; and Hancock Field ANGB, NY. AATC conducts operational test and evaluation (OT&E) for the Air Reserve Component (ARC) and other Major Commands (MAJCOMs) exercising lead command authority over a variety of ARC possessed Mission Design Series (MDS) systems and associated weapons, sensors, and support equipment. These ARC aircraft and systems are older and require low cost, off-the-shelf modernization updates to maintain combat capabilities. AATC has engineering and test responsibility for the National Guard Bureau (NGB) and Air Force Reserve Command (AFRC). In this role, AATC is responsible for working with Air Force Material Command (AFMC), system program offices (SPOs), and other related engineering offices to conduct research, development, test, and evaluation to determine the operational suitability and effectiveness of candidate developmental sensors and systems that address the modernization requirements identified in the annual Air National Guard Weapons System Modernization Priorities Book, and Air Force Reserve Modernization Book as well as requirements provided to AATC by the MAJCOMs. There are currently over 100 active projects at AATC supporting A-10, C-130, F-15, F-35, F-16, C-17, KC-135, KC-46, HH-60, HC/MC-130, MQ-9, Special Warfare (SW), Cyber, and multiple cross-platform logistics and electronic warfare (EW) capabilities. The average lifetime of most projects is six months to three years from concept approval to final report and initial fielding, but complexity may shorten or extend the amount of time required to complete the project. Expertise for each of these platforms and capability areas is required to ensure successful testing of modernization capabilities. Skill set requirements may be transferable or adjusted as projects are completed and new projects are started. Required technical expertise includes but is not limited to: operational and maintenance experience on specific platforms, expertise or familiarization with platform systems, integration and modification experience, developmental and operational test experience, airworthiness and Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) approvals, assisting the Government with technical requirements definition, cost assessment and control, executing aircraft avionics integration, systems engineering, design engineering, creating integrated logistics support such as technical orders, flight manuals, job guides, and software manuals, and program engineering coordination necessary to support ANG and AFRC modification programs. New projects may need additional expertise as they are approved in the annual United States Air Force Reserve Modernization Book and ANG Weapons Systems Modernization Priorities Book. These books are available online and identify modernization priorities and projects this PWS will support. As modernization priorities and projects are approved and funded, AATC will conduct OT&E activities to determine the validity of solutions and make fielding recommendations, as required. The contractor will support this process through all phases from concept development, test planning, test execution, and final report delivery. The ability to develop briefings, write test plans, conduct tests, and deliver comprehensive final reports is required. The contractor shall perform test planning, test execution, data analysis, test reporting, test logistics and studies/analysis for modernization installations and integration on ARC platforms which are composed of the ANG and AFRC weapons systems. In addition, the contractor shall perform specialized System Under Test (SUT) acquisition, program management, integration engineering, engineering liaison, and technology insertion to assist AATC and NGB/A5 with modernization of ARC weapons systems to include but not limited to aircraft, Joint Terminal Area Controller (JTAC) and Special Warfare, Command, Control, Communications, Computers, Intelligence, Surveillance and Reconnaissance (C4ISR), domestic operations, cyber security, logistics programs software support, and test process training support. ARC modernization efforts require avionics, mechanical, and structural modifications to include but not limited to technical requirements definition, avionics integration, systems engineering, design engineering, test support, integrated logistics engineering, studies and analyses, cybersecurity approval, prototype installations, program engineering coordination, test equipment, and technical documentation. Participation in integrated product teams (IPTs) within the Department of Defense (DoD) communities will be required to accomplish the assigned tasks. The products and support will be provided to several customers including AATC, MAJCOMs, Air Force and other DoD stakeholders to include the Aeronautical Systems Center (ASC) and Air Force Research Laboratory (AFRL) supported programs, Air Force Life Cycle Management Centers (AFLCM) program offices, and Joint Program Offices (JPO).

PURPOSE The Government is conducting market research to identify potential industry sources capable of providing solutions for a Ground-Based, Medium-Caliber Gun Weapon System that fires affordable munitions, enables defense against air and missile threats with an initial focus on subsonic cruise missiles (CM) and Unmanned Aircraft Systems (UAS) to provide persistent defense in support of United States Air Force assets. The objective of this RFI is to gather information regarding industry capability. ACQUISITION STRATEGY? The program's acquisition strategy is currently in development.? SCOPE/REQUIREMENTS The scope of this RFI is centered on solutions that strictly prioritize fifteen baseline attributes essential to operational success that can engage both cruise missiles and UAS (groups 1-5) threats in accordance with the reference documents. To effectively assess and compare air defense weapon system performance, there are fifteen critical baseline operational and technical parameters that must be analyzed in unison. These key metrics begin with the system's Salvo Probability of Kill (Pk) evaluated against both Cruise Missiles (CM) and Unmanned Aircraft Systems (UAS) Groups 1-5 at maximum range and altitude, ensuring robust lethality against diverse modern threats. The physical footprint of the engagement envelope is defined by its Effective Slant Range and Elevation Coverage, while the capacity for sustained operations is dictated by Magazine Depth and the system's ability to execute Raid Handling against saturating attacks. Furthermore, modern multi-domain operations require seamless Integrated Sensor Capability, deep C2 System Integration, and broad System Interoperability across joint networks. From an efficiency and sustainment standpoint, the system must balance its Cost Per Engagement and Manpower requirements, supported by a reliable Built-in-Test (BIT) framework for rapid diagnostics. Finally, tactical utility is rounded out by the platform's overall Transportability, stringent Weapon Safety protocols, and its comprehensive Multi-Domain Engagement Capability to counter threats across various operational environments. Fifteen Baseline Requirements: Salvo Probability of Kill (Pk) vs CM at max range and altitude Salvo Probability of Kill (Pk) vs UAS Groups 1-5 at max range and altitude Effective Slant Range Elevation Coverage Magazine Depth Raid Handling Integrated Sensor Capability C2 System Integration System Interoperability Cost Per Engagement Manpower Built-in-Test (BIT) Transportability Weapon Safety Multi-Domain Engagement Capability When designing and evaluating next-generation defense systems, the development team must navigate critical trade-offs across three primary Trade Space Attributes to balance lethality, situational awareness, and operational flexibility. First, the system must optimize Munition Performance versus Munition Cost and Gun Capability, ensuring that the interceptor's velocity, maneuverability, and terminal effects are maximized without driving the cost-per-engagement to unsustainable levels or exceeding the physical constraints of the host platform. Second, developers must carefully select the Organic Sensor Capability and Phenomenology�integrating the right mix of radar, electro-optical, infrared, or radio-frequency sensors�to ensure reliable target acquisition and tracking across varying weather conditions, environments, and countermeasure scenarios. Finally, the entire architecture must remain Rapidly Deployable, maintaining a lightweight, modular, and transportable footprint that can be swiftly projected into austere theater environments to meet emergent threats. The acquisition specifies a brand-name commercial product manufactured solely by JPS Interoperability Solutions, Inc. Under RFO competition principles, the brand-name item represents the only hardware capable of meeting the Governments minimum mission requirements without catastrophic network disruption or unlawful parallel network architectures.Conducted pursuant to RFO FAR Part 12 (Acquisition of Commercial Products and Commercial Services). The Government requires brand-name JPS Interoperability Solutions hardware and proprietary interface cabling to expand existing Radio over IP (RoIP) dispatch operations across KYARNG tactical command centers and Joint Operations Centers (JOC). All items are Commercial Off-The-Shelf (COTS).The KYARNG G6 Mission Command Division has standardized its tactical and domestic communications infrastructure on the JPS Interoperability Solutions Radio over IP (RoIP) ecosystem, currently maintaining 10 fielded JPS units, including Z-Series controllers and RSP-Z2 gateway units. The specific justifications supporting this sole source brand-name determination include: System Interoperability and DoD Instruction 8330.01 Compliance: In accordance with DoD Instruction (DoDI) 8330.01 (Interoperability of Information Technology, Including National Security Systems), managed equipment from disparate manufacturers cannot reside on the same tactical communications network without extensive laboratory testing, recertification, and separate Risk Management Framework (RMF) authority. Introducing non-JPS consoles would require establishing parallel network structures to comply with cyber directives, which is explicitly prohibited by DoDI 8330.01. Proprietary Direct Hardware and Firmware Compatibility: The requested MCC-8 and MCC-4 dispatch consoles communicate directly with fielded JPS Z-Series controllers via proprietary communications software, digital control protocols, and encryption handshakes. Furthermore, the specialized APX consolette interface cables (P/N 5961-291414-15) provide factory-engineered, direct pinout connections to KYARNGs existing fleet of Motorola APX consolette radios. Third-party cabling or non-JPS consoles introduce signaling latency, impedance mismatches, and severe audio packet loss during emergency push-to-talk dispatches. Substantial Duplication of Cost and Operational Impact: Procuring any alternative manufacturers brand would require the deinstallation and replacement of the entire existing JPS RoIP backend infrastructure, rewiring command consoles, and retraining all G6 communications personnel. This would result in substantial duplication of cost to the Government that is not expected to be recovered through competition, as well as mission failure during Defense Support of Civil Authorities (DSCA) disaster response activations. Original Equipment Manufacturer (OEM): JPS Interoperability Solutions, Inc. is the sole developer, manufacturer, and proprietary rights holder of the MCC-4, MCC-8, and Z-Series controllers. JPS sells these proprietary items directly and does not maintain third-party distributors for these specific assemblies. Microsoft 365 Data Migration Project

Statement of Work Microsoft 365 Project 1. Background Strategic Weapons Facility Pacific (SWFPAC) currently supports a legacy Microsoft Access 2003 database identified as mission-critical and in need of immediate migration. This system serves as a warehouse and inventory management solution tracking defined storage locations, personnel assignments, and two distinct categories of inventory. SWFPAC requires professional services to facilitate the migration of mission-critical data from the Access legacy database to Flank Speed, ensuring compatibility and interoperability with the Navy enterprise with minimal disruption to SWFPAC operations. 2. Scope of Work The vendor shall provide all necessary personnel, expertise, and services to design and build an application compatible with the Navy�s Microsoft 365 platform (often referred to ask �Flank Speed�) to facilitate the migration of data from an existing Microsoft Access 2003 database to Flank Speed. The final product will utilize SharePoint Online (SPO) as the primary data repository and Microsoft Power Platform (Power Apps and Power Automate) for user interfaces, relational workflows, and automated document generation. 2.1 Vendor Competency Requirements Interested vendors must provide documented evidence of successful past performance and technical competency in designing, deploying, and supporting migrations from legacy Microsoft Access systems to Microsoft 365/Power Platform environments. 2.2 Data Architecture, Test Environment, & Migration Support Due to data security protocols, the vendor will not be provided access to live data. Instead of dictating a rigid target architecture, the Government requires the vendor to evaluate the legacy Access 2003 database structure and propose an optimized target architecture. The vendor�s proposed data schema must successfully manage and relate the following core situational entities (encompassing datasets that range from <500 up to 3,000 records): Warehouse Locations (Racks/Lockers) Defined physical locations that can be assigned inventory, and subsequently assigned/issued to specific personnel. Personnel Assignments Tracking individuals assigned to specific racks, lockers, or individual pieces of equipment (handling check-in, check-out, and return states). General Gear Inventory Non-serialized bulk items categorized and inventoried by aggregates (tracking total quantities, quantities assigned out, and available quantities remaining). Serialized Gear Inventory Individually tracked items where inventory, historical status, and assignments are maintained by individual unit (serial number), distinctly from general gear. The Vendor is expected to design and implement the most efficient, scalable SPO data schema necessary to deliver a fully functional solution handling these relationships, which may include core tables, lookup lists, workflow state management, and archives. The architecture must support full data lifecycle management, ensuring that inactive core records (e.g., separated personnel, retired inventory) can be archived and removed from active views, but securely maintained for a specified timeframe to meet audit requirements prior to permanent deletion. Once the design is approved, the vendor shall construct the architecture and populate it with synthetic test data to enable rigorous User Acceptance Testing (UAT). The vendor must facilitate testing cycles, incorporate feedback, and perform any necessary reworks identified by the internal team to guarantee the solution's full operability and alignment with mission requirements. The Vendor will provide structural templates and technical guidance to the internal team. The internal team will be solely responsible for the extraction, transformation, and loading of the live Access 2003 data into the new platform. 2.3 Application, Workflow, & Security Scope Using the synthetic test data, the vendor shall develop and refine through repeat testing a unified Power Apps interface and Power Automate workflows to handle relational data linking (e.g., assigning inventory to racks, and issuing racks/inventory to personnel), automated document generation, approval routing, and comprehensive transaction logging. Forms and transaction logs must be automatically routed to designated SPO Document Libraries. Throughout the solution's development, the Vendor shall facilitate discussions with the SWFPAC internal team to define, configure, and enforce appropriate permission restrictions and user groupings across all system components (SPO Lists, Document Libraries, and Power Platform interfaces). 3. Deliverables The vendor shall provide the following deliverables according to the agreed-upon project schedule. Title Description & Acceptance Criteria D.1 System Architecture & Design Plan A comprehensive design document outlining the proposed SPO data schema. The design must ensure all core entities effectively correlate, support multiple identifying columns per entity, and detail the document library structure and proposed permission groupings/restrictions. The System Architecture and Design Plan must be approved by the Government POC prior to development. D.2 SPO Infrastructure & Migration Support Guide Construction of the approved SPO data architecture populated with vendor-generated test data. Delivery of a Migration Guide providing the SWFPAC internal team with step-by-step instructions and support mechanisms for executing the live data transfer. D.3 Data Entry & Management Interface A Power App (or customized SPO form interface) validated with test data and refined via internal team feedback, enabling users to securely add, view, edit, and archive entries across all migrated datasets. The interface must support capturing multiple identifying columns (including serial numbers where applicable) for each entity, maintain effective relational correlations, and provide adaptable sorting/filtering views for easy data retrieval during audits. Access and editing capabilities must be strictly locked down by approved permission groupings to prevent unauthorized or erroneous changes. D.4 Relational Assignment Workflows Power Automate flows enabling users to create, manage, and track relational assignments (e.g., assigning specific gear to racks/lockers, and issuing inventory/racks to personnel). Workflows must govern the full check-in, check-out, and return lifecycle, and must include data validation logic and permission lock-downs to prevent erroneous correlations or improper inventory adjustments. D.5 Approval Routing Workflows Automated workflows requiring designated approvals for specific assignment transactions to ensure accountability. Must include notification mechanisms. D.6 Automated & Manual Document Generation System capability to generate two (2) distinct types of templated documents based on list data and assignment conditions. Must include both an automatic trigger (condition-based) and a manual prompt option. D.7 Document Library Configuration Setup of three (3) distinct SPO Document Libraries: Two for storing the documents generated in D.6, and one for the transaction logs in D.8. Access must be restricted based on defined user groupings. D.8 Transaction Logging, Audit Views & Comprehensive Archival An automated logging mechanism capturing a comprehensive change history (all system changes, relational connections, check-in/out transactions, and edits) with users and timestamps identified. Logs must be locked down via permissions to prevent tampering. The system must support the secure archiving of historical transactional data as well as inactive core records (e.g., personnel, inventory), maintaining them for a designated timeframe to satisfy audit requirements before permanent removal. It must also provide adaptable list views for authorized users to retrieve and review ad-hoc audit data, and automatically generate and export an Excel format transaction report on a monthly cadence to a dedicated Document Library. D.9 As-Built Architecture Documentation Final, comprehensive documentation detailing the deployed solution, list schemas, flow logic, implemented permission restrictions/groupings, archival/retention logic, and maintenance requirements. D.10 Knowledge Transfer & Handoff A dedicated training session (and accompanying materials) for internal developers covering system maintenance, future minor edits, and active support during the internal team's live data migration phase. 4.0 Place of Performance The place of performance shall be 100% remote at the Vendor's facility. No on-site travel, base access, or physical presence at Strategic Weapons Facility Pacific (SWFPAC) is required or authorized. 5.0 Period of Performance The Period of Performance (PoP) for this effort shall be 180 calendar days from the date of contract award. 6.0 Security: All data exported from the SWFPAC environment will be scrubbed of any Controlled Unclassified Information by SWFPAC personnel prior to vendor receipt of data.
